summary: An offline admit of an EXCHANGED ticket is still silent — the sibling of TKT-269
description:
Found by the agent during TKT-269's ai-review stage, while checking the review's own question about a ticket that is both refunded and exchanged. Filed as incidental — real, out of TKT-269's scope, and not folded into it.

**The same offline gap TKT-269 just closed for refunds is still open for exchanges.**

`ticketExchanged` (`services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:208`) is consulted on **both live scan paths** — `postgres.go:332` (single-entry) and `scan.go:106` (pass) — and appears **nowhere** in `reconcile.go`.

TKT-166 / ADR-039 refuse an exchanged ticket at a live gate for a reason that is *not* the refund reason: an exchanged ticket has a **live replacement somewhere**, so admitting the original would admit the exchange twice. That is arguably a sharper failure than the refund case, because the replacement can be admitted legitimately at another gate on the same night.

Offline, an exchanged ticket is admitted and reconciliation records it as an ordinary redemption. Chain verifies clean. Nobody is told.

**The remedy is almost certainly TKT-269's, applied to the sibling fact** — the same guard position (inside the no-prior-redemption branch, below the `redeemed` lookup), the same admission-conflict alarm class, the same four-branch analysis, the same five mutation runs. Do not assume it transfers without checking: the exchange path has its own vocabulary (`exchanged` is a singleton event, and `ExchangeReplacement` semantics may differ) and the branch analysis must be redone rather than copied. TKT-269's `kind=coding` comment carries the mutation table to reuse as a template.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Reconciling an occurrence for an **exchanged** ticket owes an admission-conflict alarm, in the same transaction as the append.
- [ ] The occurrence is still recorded exactly as today — recording, not deciding (ADR-025 §D2/§D6).
- [ ] The pass, broken-chain and duplicate-admit branches are analysed explicitly, with a stated reason for each that does not alarm.
- [ ] A ticket that is **both** refunded and exchanged owes exactly **one** alarm, not two — this is the case that does not exist in TKT-269 and is the reason this cannot be a copy-paste.
- [ ] Each new test verified red against the mutation it claims to catch.

Quality gates: `make check` green; `access verify-lifecycle` green.

objective.note: An offline admit of an EXCHANGED ticket is silent. Re-verified at HEAD ad849f98: `ticketExchanged` is consulted on both live paths (postgres.go:332, scan.go:106) and appears ZERO times in reconcile.go, while TKT-269's refunded guard sits at reconcile.go:221. Sharper than the refund case: an exchanged ticket has a live replacement somewhere, so admitting the original can admit the exchange twice, and the replacement can be admitted legitimately at another gate the same night.

scope.note: IN: an exchanged guard in reconcile.go alongside the refunded one, on the same admission-conflict alarm class; the four-branch coverage TKT-269 established, INCLUDING the pass path (pass_admission_smoke_test.go:711 shows TKT-269's branch (c) covered passes, so an exchange-only single-entry fix would leave the pass path open); the refunded-AND-exchanged case. OUT: the live-gate paths (already correct since TKT-166); the voided-ticket feed (TKT-162, Done); changing the alarm schema.

uncertainties.note: Both resolved by reading the template rather than deferred. (1) One alarm or two for a ticket both refunded and exchanged? ONE — one physical admission is one conflict, and TKT-269's branch (b) test (TestReconcileRefundedDuplicateOwesExactlyOneAlarm) exists precisely because the COUNT is what constrains guard PLACEMENT: hoisting a check above the prior-redeemed lookup owes a second alarm for one occurrence. The same trap applies here and the same count assertion catches it. (2) Does the payload need a new reason? No — the admission-conflict class already means 'the chain is valid and the world disagreed with it'; the wire golden (TestWireGoldenAdmissionConflictAlarm) pins the shape and a canonical-form change would be a version migration, not a test update.

dependencies.note: No blockers. TKT-269 is Done and is the template, not a dependency; TKT-166/ADR-039 established the live-gate refusal. TKT-162 (the feed) is Done and independent.

approach.note: Add the guard inside the no-prior-redemption branch, BELOW the `redeemed` lookup — the placement TKT-269's branch (b) test pins and the placement a naive hoist gets wrong. Reuse the existing admission-conflict alarm class and `oweConflictAlarm` (reconcile.go:336). Do NOT copy TKT-269's branch analysis: redo it, because the exchange path has its own vocabulary and its own predicate (`ticketExchanged`, exchanges.go:208). Not `deferred`: this is an access-control surface, one of shaping.md's four carve-outs.

first_slice.note: The whole ticket, as TKT-269 was — one guard, one alarm class, four branches plus the combined case. Splitting single-entry from pass would ship a half-closed hole, which is the failure mode this ticket exists to correct.

success.note: Five ACs on the ticket, each testable. The discriminating evidence is per-branch mutation: delete the exchanged guard and the NEW branch tests go red while TKT-269's refunded tests stay green — a mutation caught only by the new tier is the one that is evidence (AGENTS.md). The combined refunded-AND-exchanged case asserts a COUNT of exactly one alarm, stated as the invariant rather than as an observed value: one physical admission owes one conflict alarm.

context_memo.note: governingAdrs: ADR-039-exchange-settles-the-difference.md (why an exchanged ticket is refused live — a DIFFERENT reason from the refund case); ADR-025-admission-events-and-offline-reconciliation.md (§D2/§D6 — reconciliation RECORDS, it does not decide, and the person is already inside); ADR-038-refund-reversal-ticket-voiding.md (§4 states the offline gap and hands it onward — NOTE its Consequences say the fail-open narrowing 'applies only to tickets a refund has voided', so ADR-038 does NOT cover the exchange case and this ticket must say which ADR does, or amend one); ADR-021 (name the adversary: honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence). All four verified present at HEAD. governingTests: the TKT-269 four-branch suite in occurrence_smoke_test.go (:911 onward) — in particular TestReconcileRefundedDuplicateOwesExactlyOneAlarm (:1039), which pins guard PLACEMENT via an alarm count and is the single most transferable constraint; TestPassReconcileRefundedTicketRecordsFactWithoutConflictAlarm (pass_admission_smoke_test.go:722) and branch (c) at :711, which prove the pass path is in scope; TestWireGoldenAdmissionConflictAlarm (alarm_envelope_test.go:63), a golden literal — changing a byte is a canonical-version migration, not a test update.

### ✅ Implementation readiness — PASS

Backlog review 2026-08-25, re-verified at HEAD `ad849f98`. **All eight items `met`** — the five that were `open` at filing are now closed by reading the code and TKT-269's shipped suite. Ready for Gate 1.

**The gap is confirmed at HEAD, not inherited from the filing review.** `ticketExchanged` (`exchanges.go:208`) is consulted at `postgres.go:332` and `scan.go:106` and appears **zero** times in `reconcile.go`, where TKT-269's refunded guard sits at `:221`.

**Three findings that change the work, all from reading rather than assuming.** The ticket said "the remedy is almost certainly TKT-269's, applied to the sibling fact — do not assume it transfers without checking." Checked:

1. **The pass path is in scope, and the ticket does not say so.** TKT-269's branch (c) covered passes (`pass_admission_smoke_test.go:711`, `TestPassReconcileRefundedTicketRecordsFactWithoutConflictAlarm`). An exchange guard added only to single-entry reconciliation leaves the pass path silent — the same half-closed hole this ticket exists to correct.

2. **The alarm COUNT is the assertion that bites, not "an alarm exists."** `TestReconcileRefundedDuplicateOwesExactlyOneAlarm` (`:1039`) exists because branch (b) already owed an alarm before TKT-269, so presence proves nothing; what it constrains is **placement** — hoisting the check above the prior-redeemed lookup owes a *second* alarm for one occurrence. That trap transfers exactly, and it answers the ticket's open question: a ticket both refunded and exchanged owes **one** alarm. One physical admission is one conflict.

3. **No ADR currently covers this case.** ADR-038 §4 states the offline gap, but its Consequences say the narrowing "applies only to tickets a **refund** has voided." So the exchange case has no governing decision — the ticket must either amend ADR-038 or say plainly which ADR governs. Per `shaping.md`, an honest mémo names that rather than citing a decision that does not reach the case.

**Recommend NOT `risk:low`** — an access-control surface, four branches plus a combined case, and an ADR question to settle.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna`** (codex `task`, effort high, read-only) per `config.models.plan`. Job `task-mt9o4klz-ml6iun`, 15428 bytes, conclusive.

Briefed from the ticket and the context-mémo, with the governing ADRs and governing tests re-resolved by me against HEAD `13dc1305` rather than inherited from the shaping snapshot. The brief stated the ticket's central trap up front — that the remedy *looks* like TKT-269's and must not be assumed to transfer.

---

# TKT-270 execution plan

The branch is clean and currently matches `origin/main` at `13dc1305`.

## Verified gap

- `ticketExchanged` checks only `event_type='exchanged'` in [`exchanges.go:208`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:208).
- Both live paths already consult it: single-entry in [`postgres.go:332`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/postgres.go:332), pass scanning in [`scan.go:106`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/scan.go:106).
- Reconciliation currently checks only `ticketRefunded` in [`reconcile.go:221`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go:221).
- The existing guard is inside the no-prior-redemption branch, after the append and below the redeemed lookup. The relevant ordering is [`reconcile.go:135`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go:135), [`reconcile.go:164`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go:164), [`reconcile.go:188`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go:188), and [`reconcile.go:221`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go:221).

## DoD

1. A reconciled exchanged single-entry ticket:
   - records one ordinary `redeemed` event using the occurrence ID and device time;
   - returns `ReconcileRecorded`;
   - owes exactly one `platform.access.admission-conflict.alarm`;
   - does not create `duplicate_admit`.

2. A refunded-and-exchanged ticket owes exactly one alarm for one physical admission.

   Invariant: one physical offline admission produces at most one admission-conflict alarm, regardless of how many commercial voiding facts apply.

3. The alarm and lifecycle append commit atomically.

4. Pass reconciliation records `entry` or `exit` only and owes no immutable admission-conflict alarm.

5. Broken-chain reconciliation records quarantine data and owes no admission-conflict alarm. The integrity alarm class remains responsible for the broken chain.

6. A duplicate single-entry reconciliation still creates exactly one `duplicate_admit` and exactly one new alarm for that occurrence. It must not receive an additional alarm merely because the ticket is exchanged.

7. The schema-1 alarm envelope remains unchanged. [`alarm_envelope_test.go:63`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/alarm_envelope_test.go:63) must remain untouched and green.

8. `access verify-lifecycle` continues to pass. Every new lifecycle event must use `appendLifecycle`, whose coverage requirement is enforced in [`lifecycle_verify.go:118`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/lifecycle_verify.go:118).

## Exact implementation

In [`reconcile.go:221`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go:221), keep the existing placement and load both independent facts:

```go
refunded, err := ticketRefunded(ctx, tx, in.TicketID)
if err != nil {
    return ReconcileResult{}, err
}

exchanged, err := ticketExchanged(ctx, tx, in.TicketID)
if err != nil {
    return ReconcileResult{}, err
}

if refunded || exchanged {
    if err = p.oweConflictAlarm(...); err != nil {
        return ReconcileResult{}, err
    }
}
```

The single `if refunded || exchanged` is intentional. Two independent alarm branches would fail AC4 by owing two alarms for the same admission.

Keep this block:

- inside the no-prior-redemption branch;
- after the `redeemed` lookup;
- after `appendLifecycle`;
- after `verifyTicketChain`;
- below the pass split.

The three placement constraints remain the same:

- Above the redeemed lookup would add a second alarm on the duplicate path.
- Above the pass split would mint an immutable conflict for a pass, although pass conflicts are derived and revisable under ADR-025 §D2.
- Above `verifyTicketChain` would classify a broken chain as an admission conflict instead of leaving it to the integrity alarm path.

The existing `ticketCommerciallyVoid` query in [`exchanges.go:197`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:197) is not the right abstraction here. It is the broad source-ticket eligibility check used by `SwitchExchange` before voiding tickets, at [`exchanges.go:151`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:151). Reconciliation needs the separate exchange verdict, just as it separately uses `ticketRefunded`.

## Exchange seeding

Add an `exchangeOwnTicket` helper to [`occurrence_smoke_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/occurrence_smoke_test.go).

For `issueTicket`, the source is already a one-ticket order because [`lifecycle_smoke_test.go:30`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/lifecycle_smoke_test.go:30) gives the ticket its own order ID.

The helper should:

1. Create a new replacement order ID.
2. Build one replacement ticket with the existing [`replacementTickets` helper](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges_smoke_test.go:20).
3. Call:

```go
st.SwitchExchange(ctx, SwitchExchangeInput{
    EventID:       uuid.New(),
    ExchangeID:    uuid.New(),
    SourceOrderID: s.id.OrderID,
    OrganizerID:   s.id.OrganizerID,
    Tickets:       replacementTickets(newOrderID, s.id.OrganizerID, uuid.New(), 1),
})
```

This satisfies the real `SwitchExchangeInput` fields defined in [`exchanges.go:65`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:65). One source ticket and one replacement ticket satisfy the whole-order rule at [`exchanges.go:140`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:140).

Do not insert an `exchanged` row directly. `SwitchExchange` appends each source `exchanged` event through [`exchanges.go:175`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:175), and issues replacement tickets through [`exchanges.go:184`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:184). Both routes ultimately use the signed append path.

### Refunded-and-exchanged construction

This state is constructible through the current Access store paths:

1. Issue the one-ticket source order.
2. Call `SwitchExchange`.
3. Call `refundOwnTicket`, which invokes `RefundOrderTickets(..., quantity 1)` against the original source order.

The refund path only excludes tickets already refunded, as shown by [`refunds.go:117`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/refunds.go:117). It does not reject an existing `exchanged` event. The exchange must happen first. Reversing the order fails because `SwitchExchange` uses the combined commercial-void check and refuses already-voided source tickets at [`exchanges.go:151`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:151).

Both events still enter through `appendLifecycle`: refund at [`refunds.go:167`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/refunds.go:167), exchange at [`exchanges.go:175`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/exchanges.go:175).

## Files to touch

- [`services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/reconcile.go)
  - Add the exchange fact lookup.
  - Change the guard to one `refunded || exchanged` condition.
  - Update the `oweConflictAlarm` caller comment to include exchanged tickets.

- [`services/access/internal/store/occurrence_smoke_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/occurrence_smoke_test.go)
  - Add `exchangeOwnTicket`.
  - Add single-entry exchanged, duplicate, broken-chain, both-voided, and atomicity tests.

- [`services/access/internal/store/pass_admission_smoke_test.go`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/pass_admission_smoke_test.go)
  - Add the exchanged-pass test.

Do not modify migrations, `exchanges.go`, `refunds.go`, or the alarm envelope.

## Test plan and seams

Add these tests.

### Single-entry positive branch

`TestReconcileExchangedTicketRecordsRedemptionAndOwesAlarm`

Seed with `issueTicket` and `exchangeOwnTicket`. Assert the exchanged event exists before reconciliation, then assert:

- `ReconcileRecorded`;
- one `redeemed` event keyed by the occurrence;
- device time preserved;
- no `duplicate_admit`;
- one conflict alarm;
- lifecycle verification succeeds.

The exchanged-event precondition makes the exchange seed load-bearing.

### Duplicate branch

`TestReconcileExchangedDuplicateOwesExactlyOneAdditionalAlarm`

Because `SwitchExchange` refuses an already-admitted source ticket, construct the state in this order:

1. Exchange the source ticket.
2. Reconcile occurrence A. This records `redeemed` and owes the first exchange alarm.
3. Reconcile occurrence B. This must append one `duplicate_admit` and owe exactly one additional alarm.

Measure the alarm count before and after occurrence B. The expected delta is one. Moving the exchange guard above the redeemed lookup would produce two new alarms for occurrence B and fail this test.

Removing the exchange guard entirely will not make this test red, because the duplicate path already owns one alarm. That is expected. This test proves placement, not guard presence.

### Broken-chain branch

`TestReconcileExchangedBrokenChainRecordsQuarantineWithoutConflictAlarm`

Seed through `SwitchExchange`, assert the exchanged event exists, then corrupt the chain using the existing `corruptChain` helper. Reconcile and assert:

- `ReconcileRecorded`;
- one quarantine-side occurrence;
- no `redeemed` or `duplicate_admit`;
- zero admission-conflict alarms.

Moving the exchange guard above `verifyTicketChain` must make the test fail by creating an admission-conflict alarm.

### Pass branch

`TestPassReconcileExchangedTicketRecordsFactWithoutConflictAlarm`

Use `issueAndSeed` with a multi-entry policy, exchange the ticket through `SwitchExchange`, assert the exchanged event exists, then reconcile an entry.

Assert:

- `ReconcileRecorded`;
- one `entry`;
- no `redeemed`;
- no `duplicate_admit`;
- zero admission-conflict alarms.

Moving the guard above the pass split must fail this test. The exchange seed is load-bearing because an ordinary pass reconciliation would satisfy all of these assertions.

This follows the existing refunded-pass test at [`pass_admission_smoke_test.go:722`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/pass_admission_smoke_test.go:722), whose comment correctly explains why its voiding seed must be observed.

### Both-voided branch

`TestReconcileRefundedAndExchangedTicketOwesExactlyOneAlarm`

Construct the state with:

```text
issueTicket
SwitchExchange
refundOwnTicket
ReconcileAdmission
```

Assert both `refunded` and `exchanged` exist before reconciliation, then assert one ordinary redemption and exactly one admission-conflict alarm.

Mutating the implementation into two independent `if` blocks must make this test fail with an alarm count of two. The expected count comes from the requirement, not from observing the implementation.

### Atomicity

`TestReconcileExchangedAlarmAndAppendCommitTogether`

Reuse the existing database seam from [`occurrence_smoke_test.go:1117`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/occurrence_smoke_test.go:1117):

- create a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `lifecycle_integrity_alarm_outbox`;
- make it raise an error;
- reconcile an exchanged ticket;
- assert reconciliation fails;
- assert no `redeemed` event committed;
- assert no conflict alarm committed;
- assert the prior `exchanged` event remains.

This is the correct seam because the mechanism is the database transaction, not a mock callback. It catches removal of the exchange guard and any split-transaction implementation.

## Mutation evidence

Before the final gate, run the new tests against these mutations independently:

- Delete the exchanged guard. The exchanged positive and atomicity tests must go red. The existing TKT-269 refunded tests must stay green.
- Move the exchange guard above the redeemed lookup. The exchanged duplicate test must go red.
- Move it above the pass split. The exchanged-pass test must go red.
- Move it above `verifyTicketChain`. The broken-chain test must go red.
- Replace `refunded || exchanged` with two alarm-owning branches. The both-voided test must go red.
- Delete the exchange seed from each negative test. Its explicit exchanged-event precondition must go red.

Run mutation tests separately from the final gate. Do not edit tracked files while `make check` is running.

## ADR position

ADR-025 §§D2 and D6 governs this change. It says reconciliation records admissions that already happened, and the admission-conflict alarm is for a valid trace that disagreed with the offline admission. The relevant implementation contract is at [`ADR-025:166`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/docs/adr/ADR-025-admission-events-and-offline-reconciliation.md:166).

ADR-039 explains why an exchanged ticket is refused live, at [`ADR-039:56`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/docs/adr/ADR-039-exchange-settles-the-difference.md:56), but does not define reconciliation.

ADR-038 does not govern the exchange case. Its offline gap and its narrow fail-open consequence explicitly apply only to refunded tickets, at [`ADR-038:83`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/docs/adr/ADR-038-refund-reversal-ticket-voiding.md:83) and [`ADR-038:220`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/docs/adr/ADR-038-refund-reversal-ticket-voiding.md:220).

No ADR amendment is required unless the project wants ADR-039 or ADR-025 to name exchange revocation explicitly. The implementation should not cite ADR-038 for this behavior.

Per ADR-021, this remains honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence. A database writer can remove or alter the voiding facts; the chain only makes that detectable against an adversary who cannot re-sign it. See [`ADR-021:44`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/docs/adr/ADR-021-ticket-lifecycle-trail-integrity.md:44).

## Risks and open decisions

- The Access store currently permits `SwitchExchange` followed by `RefundOrderTickets` on the source order. Commerce may consider that state invalid, but changing refund authorization is outside TKT-270. The AC4 test should use the existing real Access paths and should not hand-insert lifecycle rows.
- The common alarm envelope does not identify whether the conflict came from a refund or exchange. Do not add a cause field here. That would change the ADR-017 payload contract and break the golden at [`alarm_envelope_test.go:71`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/access/internal/store/alarm_envelope_test.go:71).
- I did not execute the smoke suite, mutation runs, `make check`, or `access verify-lifecycle` in this read-only planning pass. The exchange-plus-refund construction and alarm counts still need execution in the implementation run.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
**Adversarial critique by `main-agent`** (per `config.models.planReview`; `plan: gpt-5.6-luna` ≠ `planReview: main-agent`). Every file, symbol, line and seam the draft names was checked at HEAD `13dc1305`, and the two constructions it depends on were traced through the real code rather than accepted.

## Summary

**Accept the draft's implementation and test plan with three amendments.** It did the thing the brief demanded and that this ticket exists to force: it **redid** the analysis instead of porting TKT-269's, and it caught something on its own that I would have flagged — that the duplicate-branch test proves *placement*, not *guard presence*. That honesty is worth more than the finding.

---

## Verified — accepted as written

**The gap, all four claims re-derived.** `ticketExchanged` at `exchanges.go:208` tests `event_type='exchanged'` alone ✅; consulted at `postgres.go:332` and `scan.go:106` ✅; absent from `reconcile.go` ✅; TKT-269's guard sits at `reconcile.go:221` inside the no-prior-redemption branch, below the `redeemed` lookup ✅.

**The `refunded || exchanged` single-condition shape is right, and for the stated reason.** One `oweConflictAlarm` call site means AC4's count is one **by construction**, not by observation. Two independent alarm-owning branches would owe two for one physical admission. This is the correct reading of why TKT-269's branch (b) test exists.

**`ticketCommerciallyVoid` (`exchanges.go:197`) correctly rejected as the predicate here.** I read it: it tests `IN ('refunded','exchanged')` and is `SwitchExchange`'s source-eligibility check (`exchanges.go:151`). Using it in reconcile would collapse two verdicts the codebase deliberately keeps separate — and would make the AC4 test vacuous, since one predicate cannot distinguish the both-voided case from either alone. The draft spotted the trap the brief planted. ✅

**Both constructions traced through the real code and both hold.**
- *Exchange-then-refund is the only viable order.* `SwitchExchange` refuses an already-voided source (`exchanges.go:151-158`, `ErrSourceTicketsAlreadyVoided`), so refund-first is impossible. Conversely `RefundOrderTickets` selects on `refundThatVoided` alone (`refunds.go:120-131`) — an `exchanged` ticket is still "free" and refundable. **The both-voided state is constructible.** ✅
- *`SwitchExchangeInput`* is `{EventID, ExchangeID, SourceOrderID, OrganizerID, Tickets}` (`exchanges.go:66-78`) — the draft's call matches exactly ✅. `replacementTickets(order, org, slot, n)` exists at `exchanges_smoke_test.go:20` ✅. `corruptChain` at `lifecycle_smoke_test.go:57` ✅.

**Seeding through the real path.** `SwitchExchange` appends `exchanged` via `appendLifecycle` (`exchanges.go:175`) ✅. The draft's "do not hand-insert" instruction is load-bearing, not boilerplate: `access verify-lifecycle` runs in the gate and a direct insert reads as tampering (AGENTS.md).

**The ADR position is correct and is the most valuable non-obvious finding in the draft.** I verified it independently: ADR-038's Consequences say the fail-open narrowing *"applies only to tickets a refund has voided"* (`ADR-038:222-224`) — so **ADR-038 does not cover this**. And `grep -n "offline\|reconcil" docs/adr/ADR-039*.md` returns **nothing**: ADR-039 explains the live refusal and says nothing about reconciliation. The draft's conclusion — ADR-025 §D2/§D6 governs, no amendment strictly required, and **the implementation must not cite ADR-038 for this behaviour** — is right. Note the code comment at `reconcile.go:203-226` currently cites ADR-038 §4 for the refunded case, which remains correct for refunds; the new comment must not extend that citation to exchanges.

**Not adding a cause field to the alarm envelope.** Correct: it would change the ADR-017 payload contract and break the golden at `alarm_envelope_test.go:63`. A canonical-form change is a version migration, not a test update.

## AMENDMENT 1 — the pass mutation as stated is not runnable; say what the test actually pins

The draft says the pass test's mutation is *"move the guard above the pass split"*. Read `reconcile.go:163-186`: the pass branch **`return`s** — it appends the direction event, calls `evaluatePolicyAlarms`, commits, and returns. A guard at the refunded position is **already unreachable for passes**, so "move it above the split" is not a small edit; it is relocating the guard into a different control-flow region.

That does not make the test worthless — it makes its claim different from the draft's, and the difference matters because AGENTS.md's rule is to ask what each test would catch:

- What it **actually** pins: any future implementation that owes an admission-conflict alarm on a pass reconciliation — a guard hoisted before the pass split, or a well-meaning "alarm on every voided ticket" refactor.
- What it **cannot** catch: deleting the exchanged guard from its correct position, which leaves this test green because the pass path never reaches it.

**Required in the plan:** state that distinction in the test's comment, exactly as `pass_admission_smoke_test.go:711-721` does for the refunded case — that comment is a model, and it exists because TKT-269's own plan critique forced the question. And keep the draft's instruction that **the exchange seed is load-bearing**: without it the assertions are satisfied by any pass reconcile and the test duplicates `TestPassReconcileRecordsFactualEntryExitOnly`. The exchanged-event precondition assertion is what makes the seed observable.

## AMENDMENT 2 — the discriminating mutation must be run, and it is the shaping's own success criterion

The draft's mutation list is good and I accept all six. But the shaped ticket names one specific run as **the** evidence, and the draft does not call it out as distinct:

> **Delete the exchanged guard: the NEW branch tests go red while TKT-269's refunded tests stay GREEN.**

Both halves are the point. Red-only proves the new tests observe something; *refunded-stays-green* proves they observe the **new** mechanism rather than re-testing the old one. AGENTS.md: a mutation caught by a tier that already existed proves the mechanism is live, not that your test caught it.

**Required in the plan:** run it as one experiment and record **both** columns in the coding stage comment. And per the draft's own observation, record explicitly that the **duplicate test stays green** under guard deletion — that is expected, it pins placement not presence, and an unexplained green there will read as a hole to the next reviewer.

## AMENDMENT 3 — assert the invariant, not the observed number

AC4 asserts a count, and AGENTS.md is sharpest here: *a green test can assert the DEFECT as correct, and mutation testing cannot catch that.* An assertion written by observing what the code produced pins the behaviour, not the rule.

**Required in the plan:** the both-voided test's failure message states the invariant in one sentence without naming the implementation —

> *one physical offline admission owes exactly one admission-conflict alarm, however many commercial voiding facts apply to the ticket*

— and the expected `1` is derived from that sentence, not from a run. The draft already words the invariant correctly in its DoD §2; it just needs to land **in the assertion's message**, where the next reader meets it.

## Pre-mortem — it is three weeks later and this did not hold

- **Most likely: a new voiding fact is added and only the live paths learn about it.** This ticket closes exchange the way TKT-269 closed refund, one fact at a time, and nothing structurally prevents a third from repeating the gap. The draft already specifies this; keep it, and make the helper `t.Fatal` on a seed error rather than tolerate it.
